summary: The note surveys the technical side of wood-fired oven baking as of autumn 2023, drawing on talks, demonstrations and posts by various chefs and experts. It covers oven design and thermal mass, the three modes of heat transfer, wood choice and fire-starting, temperature control, and techniques for bread, pizza, pastry and slow roasting. It closes with residual heat use, modern temperature-measurement tools, and the unpredictable nature of fire.
one_line: A technical overview of wood-fired oven baking in 2023, covering oven design, heat transfer, wood choice, temperature control and techniques for bread, pizza, pastry and meats.
key_facts: Oven builder Marco Bianchi unveiled his latest wood-fired oven design at the International Culinary Congress on September 15, 2023.
Wood-fired ovens have a dome shape and are typically built from brick, clay, or stone, which have high thermal mass and release heat gradually for even cooking.
Thermal engineer Dr. Emily Frost led a workshop on October 3, 2023, explaining that heat transfers by conduction, convection, and radiation.
In a wood-fired oven, conduction is the oven floor heating the bottom of a pizza, convection circulates hot air for uniform temperatures, and radiation evenly browns the food surface.
Matteo Rossi, sommelier and wood-fire expert, said at an October 20, 2023 symposium that hardwoods like oak, maple, and birch are preferred for slow, consistent burn and subtle aromas.
Oven temperatures range from 300°F for slow-roasted meats to upwards of 800°F for crispy pizzas.
Chef Anita Nguyen demonstrated on September 30, 2023 pushing the fire to the oven's sides, using hotter areas for quick-cooking items and cooler areas for slower dishes.
Artisan baker Lucas Weber discussed the 'soaking' phase, when the oven's masonry is fully saturated with heat, in his September 22, 2023 masterclass on bread.
Pastry chef Sophia Bellini wrote in an October 10, 2023 blog post that pastries need timing and rotational baking to get the right heat without burning.
Pitmaster Aaron Clarke demonstrated on October 29, 2023 that residual oven heat, which can stay high for hours, suits slow-roasting meats after the initial high-heat phase.
Chef Julien Dupont lectured on November 8, 2023 about using embers and residual heat to bake or dry ingredients as the fire dies down.
A tech panel on September 18, 2023 discussed infrared thermometers and heat-sensing cameras as tools for monitoring oven temperature.
Artisanal pizza maker Giorgio Conti said in a September 25, 2023 interview that no two fires are the same.
